ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an "L"-shaped plate B is at rest on the ground, and a small block A is located at point $O^{\prime}$ on plate B. The right side of point $O^{\prime}$ is rough, while the left side is smooth. A small ball of mass $M$ is suspended by an inextensible light rope at point $O$ directly above point $O^{\prime}$, with the rope in a horizontal and taut state. The ball is released from rest, swings down to its lowest point, and collides with block A. After the collision, the direction of the ball's velocity remains the same as before the collision, and it begins to perform simple harmonic motion. Block A slides along the plate with a velocity $v_{0}$ until it undergoes an elastic collision with the left barrier of plate B. After some time, when block A returns to the point directly below $O$, its velocity relative to the ground reduces to zero, and at this moment, the ball just reaches its highest point for the first time. The mass of block A is $m_{\mathrm{A}}=0.1\mathrm{kg}$, the mass of plate B is $m_{\mathrm{B}}=0.3\mathrm{kg}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between A and B is $\mu_{1}=0.4$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between B and the ground is $\mu_{2}=0.225$, $v_{0}=4\mathrm{m/s}$, and the gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m/s}^{2}$. Throughout the entire process, block A remains on plate B, all collision times are negligible, and air resistance is ignored.

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity $v_{\mathrm{A}}$ of A after it collides with the baffle of B?
2. What is the amount of heat $Q$ generated by friction between B and the ground during the motion? (The result should be rounded to two significant figures.)
3. What is the length $L$ of the pendulum? ($\pi^{2}{=}10$)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an L-shaped plate B resting on a horizontal ground surface. A vertical baffle is at the left end of B. Block A is initially on the horizontal top of B at the point marked O′, which lies directly below the suspension point O. A pendulum bob labeled ball is attached to O by a light string; initially the string is horizontal to the right, and a dashed arc indicates the bob swings downward to collide with A near O′. The left side of O′ on the plate is the smooth part leading to the baffle, and the right side is the rough part. Reasoning: Take rightward as positive and take the fixed ground point directly below O, initially O′, as x=0. After the ball hits A, A moves left with speed v0=4 m/s on the smooth left part, so B stays at rest until A reaches the left baffle. 1. Elastic collision with the baffle/plate: Treat the collision as a 1D elastic collision between A, mass mA=0.1 kg, initial velocity uA=-4 m/s, and B, mass mB=0.3 kg, initial velocity uB=0. Then vA=((mA-mB)/(mA+mB))uA=(-0.2/0.4)(-4)=2 m/s, vB=(2mA/(mA+mB))uA=(0.2/0.4)(-4)=-2 m/s. So the magnitude of A’s velocity after hitting the baffle is 2 m/s. 2. Motion after the baffle collision: During the smooth-stage return, A moves right at constant ground velocity 2 m/s. B slides left under ground friction only. The ground friction magnitude is f2=μ2(mA+mB)g=0.225×0.4×10=0.9 N, so B’s acceleration is aB=f2/mB=0.9/0.3=3 m/s² rightward. If t is measured from just after the baffle collision, vB=-2+3t, xB=-2t+1.5t². When A reaches the rough boundary O′ on the plate, the rough-stage begins. On the rough part, A is sliding right relative to B, so friction on A is leftward and aA=-μ1g=-0.4×10=-4 m/s². At the final specified instant, A is at x=0 and vA=0. Since A enters the rough part with vA=2 m/s, the rough-stage duration is 0=2-4t, so t=0.5 s. The displacement of A during this rough stage is Δx=2(0.5)-0.5×4×(0.5)²=0.5 m. Therefore A must have entered the rough part at x=-0.5 m. This means xB=-0.5 m at the end of the smooth stage. Hence -2t+1.5t²=-0.5, which gives t=1/3 s or 1 s. The valid one before B stops is t=1/3 s. Thus the smooth-stage ground sliding distance of B is 0.5 m, and B’s speed then is vB=-2+3(1/3)=-1 m/s. In the rough stage, while B is still sliding left, friction from A and ground friction both act rightward on B. The friction from A is f1=μ1mAg=0.4×0.1×10=0.4 N. Thus B’s rightward acceleration is aB=(f1+f2)/mB=(0.4+0.9)/0.3=13/3 m/s². Starting from speed 1 m/s leftward, B stops after an additional sliding distance s=v²/(2a)=1/[2(13/3)]=3/26 m. So the total ground-sliding distance of B is 0.5+3/26=8/13 m. The heat generated by friction between B and the ground is Q=f2 s=0.9×8/13=0.5538... J≈0.55 J. 3. Pendulum length: Let d be the distance from initial O′ to the left baffle. During the smooth-stage return, A and the moving boundary meet after 1/3 s, so -d+2t=xB=-0.5 at t=1/3, or equivalently d=4t-1.5t²=4/3-1/6=7/6 m. Thus the time from the initial ball-A collision to A reaching the baffle is t0=d/v0=(7/6)/4=7/24 s. The time from the initial ball-A collision until A finally returns to x=0 with zero velocity is therefore t_total=7/24+1/3+1/2=7/24+8/24+12/24=27/24=9/8 s. The ball starts simple harmonic motion from its lowest point after collision and first reaches its highest point after one quarter period, so T/4=9/8, hence T=9/2 s. For a pendulum, T=2π√(L/g). Therefore L=gT²/(4π²)=10×(81/4)/(4π²). Using π²=10, L=(810/4)/40=81/16 m. Final answer: vA=2 m/s, Q≈0.55 J, L=81/16 m.
